{{Wireless adapter |brand=Foxconn |model=MIC-A |revision=2 |upc= |ean= |asin= |price= |est_release_date= |fcc_date=09/02/2011 |manuf_country=China |is_manuf=Yes |manuf= |manuf_model= |manuf_rev= |if=USB (non-standard connector) |if_bus_version=2.0 |vendor_id= |device_id= |subvendor_id= |subdevice_id= |fcc_id=MCLMICA2 |ic_id=2878D-MICA2 |chip1_brand=Broadcom |chip1_model=BCM4319;BCM4319XKUBG; |flags= |ant_conn=U.FL |802dot11_protocols=an |txchains=1 |rxchains=1 |sstreams=1 |oui= |lin_driver= |win_driver= }} *This device is the 5GHz wireless module used in ''Nintendo'' Wii U gamepads. :It is visible [http://www.ifixit.com/Teardown/Nintendo+Wii+U+Teardown/11796/3 in '''iFixit''''s teardown].
The Wii U gamepads use [[wikipedia:Miracast|Miracast]] to display video generated on the Wii U console.. :which is streamed over the Wi-Fi Direct connection established by this module.
This device uses a '''SiGe''' 5008L / '''[[Skyworks]]''' SE5008L :(5GHz WLAN Switch/LNA Front End Module).
